newsitem.title: INDIA: India SOL sees higher exports in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: India SOL sees higher exports in 1996/97.

text.p: India's SOL Pharmaceuticals Ltd said it expected 1996/97 (April-March) exports at 1.5 billion rupees, up from 1.03 billion rupees in the year ago period.
"The company has started exporting commercial volumes of the third generation antibiotic cefaclor," SOL chairman C. Chandrasekara Reddy told shareholders in a report.

"Cefaclor and its intermediates, for which the quality and markets have already been established, will contribute to a great extent to the export turnover for the year 1996/97 as already memoranda of understanding for supply have been signed with Korean and European companies," he said.
SOL also expected a substantial increase in exports of antibacterial sulphamethoxazole to the United States, where price realisations are substantially higher, he said.
He said SOL was the first Indian venture in Vietnam to receive an investment licence and sign a joint venture agreement with a leading pharmaceutical company.
He did not give financial or other details.
SOL Pharmaceuticals was also pursuing a joint venture proposal in Mexico, Reddy said.
SOL is one of India's major pharmaceutical firms operating from the southern city of Hyderabad.
